# Run ledger — P26.15 (EU tender sweep via TED Search API)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P26.15__eu-tender-sweep.md` (SOURCES.14) — the EU
  procurement surface. US procurement is live at municipal (P26.10) and
  federal (P26.14) tiers; TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) is the EU
  equivalent — a public **keyless** Search API over OJ S contract notices
  covering ~30 countries where Frontex, Europol, national police forces,
  and municipalities publish surveillance-relevant tenders.
- **Branch:** `devin/p26-15-eu-tenders` — stacked on
  `devin/p26-14-federal-procurement` (PR #106). Implementation head:
  `af8b878`.
- **Date:** 2026-09-18. Same GCP posture as P26.8–P26.14: user account
  `14stevevitali@gmail.com` on `zeta-medley-508121-u7`; per-job upserts
  (`gcloud run jobs create`), never `scheduled-ops.sh --apply` (host ADC
  file corrupt, as recorded). Local Docker unresponsive — the hosted image
  was built with **Cloud Build** (`ops/Dockerfile`, repo-root context).

## What landed

### 1. Sweep plan as data — `procurement_vocab.toml` (+~255 lines)

- `[ted_eu_sweep]` — **11 reviewed English keyword slices** (CCTV,
  surveillance camera/system, video surveillance, ANPR/license-plate
  family, facial recognition, biometric, drone/UAV, acoustic gunshot,
  predictive policing, body-worn camera, cell-site simulator) plus **10
  verified CPV slices** (surveillance/security-equipment codes incl.
  32323500 video-surveillance systems, 35125000 surveillance systems,
  79714000 CCTV services, …) — one `PAGE_NUMBER` page each (`limit=250`,
  the API's page cap), `onlyLatestVersions`, `scope=ALL`, a rolling
  `publication-date>=` bound carried **in the POST body** (never in claim
  identity). The Expert-Search queries are verbatim TED syntax
  (`FT~"…"`, `classification-cpv=…`, `publication-date>=YYYYMMDD`).
- `predicate_allowlist` +`place_of_performance` +`country` +`title`;
  `vocab_version` → `2026.09.18-p26.15`. `ted_eu` added to the
  procurement source role so `ProcurementConnector` serves it.
- `[ted_eu_sweep.country_map]` — the reviewed alpha-3→alpha-2 map for
  `buyer-country` normalization (P26.9 `iso.3166_1_alpha2` scheme).

### 2. Connector — `procurement.py` (+~630 lines)

- `ted_eu_search_targets()` generates **21 bounded POST targets**
  (11 keyword + 10 CPV) at plan-version `2026.09.18.1`; `live_targets.toml`
  carries one additional baseline seed slice → 22 slices per run. Every
  target URL carries `#sig-slice=<id>` — a fragment is never transmitted
  (RFC 7230); it exists so each capture's recorded `source_uri` names the
  exact slice, and the fetch record's per-request outcomes are per-slice
  outcomes. The verbatim `post_body` dict rides the target row and is sent
  as the JSON request body through `PoliteFetcher` (one request per
  target, counted once; a refusal is recorded and never re-probed).
- TED response handling: `{"notices": [...], "totalNoticeCount": N,
  "iterationNextToken": …}` envelope; fail-closed shape checks
  (`ContentDrift` on a non-object envelope / non-list `notices`); an empty
  `notices` list is an honest empty slice, not an error.
- `_ted_i18n_values`/`_ted_first_text`/`_ted_first_seq` — TED's i18n field
  shape (`{lang: text|[texts]}`) flattened deterministically (eng first,
  then sorted languages); a notice supplying no English text still yields
  its own verbatim literal.
- `extract()` routes a TED search payload to `procurement_notice` raw
  records carrying slice provenance (query, query_kind, ted_keyword /
  cpv_code, page, limit, plan_version, capture digest) + one
  `ted_eu_slice` outcome row per capture (`items_count`,
  `total_notice_count`, `truncated`) — run-record data, not a claim.
- `_normalize_ted_notice()` emits the typed surface: `external_id`
  (publication-number), `notice_type`, `title`, `buyer` + `seller`
  (verbatim `winner-name` — the §11.11 seller predicate, only on award
  notices), `country` (verbatim alpha-3 `raw_value`, reviewed-map alpha-2
  `candidate_identifier` — an unmapped code keeps its verbatim literal
  and fabricates nothing), `amount` (`total-value` + currency verbatim),
  `posted_date`, `response_deadline`, `description`, `products`
  (verbatim `classification-cpv` codes — the notice's product
  classification), `place_of_performance` (verbatim NUTS/city literals —
  recorded as stated, never emitted as ISO 3166-2 identifiers),
  `matched_keyword` (verbatim literal slice + byte-range-into-field
  locator; the slice's query rides as provenance only — a query term not
  found verbatim in the notice is NEVER asserted), and
  `lifecycle_transition` (`cn-*` → rfp_issued, `can-*` → awarded — the
  verbatim notice-type is the lifecycle signal). Part VIII tokens in
  emitted literals are suppressed at the claim surface. **No deployment
  predicates anywhere** — `deployment_exists`/`device_count`/
  `camera_count` remain in `forbidden_predicate_genres`.

### 3. Rights — `ted_eu` flipped under GL-GATE-06

The pre-registered `ted_eu` census stub was expanded and flipped
`ingestion_permitted=true` under the GL-GATE-06 delegated blanket
disposition — the SIMAP legal notice resolves verbatim:

- OJ S procurement notices "can be freely reused, for commercial or
  non-commercial purposes" (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU).
- SIMAP editorial content is CC BY 4.0 ("provided appropriate credit is
  given"); system metadata is CC0 1.0.

→ `CC-BY-4.0` with recorded attribution; `custody_posture=REFERENCE`,
`compact_status=public_terms_only`. Verbatim packet:
`docs/build/reports/rights/ted_eu.md`. Registry: 198 sources
(the stub was already counted), 76 → **77 loadable**.

### 4. Wiring

- `api_allowlist.toml`: `api.ted.europa.eu` `/v3/` API-mode entry —
  documented keyless public API, reviewed budget 30 req/min vs the
  published 700 req/min fair-use limit. `api.ted.europa.eu/robots.txt`
  answers 404 (no policy exists, RFC 9309 §2.3.1.4) — API mode governs.
- `live_targets.toml`: `[ted_eu]` `kind=procurement_api` seed slice.
- `ops/cadence.toml`: `sig-ingest-ted-eu` / `sig-sched-ted-eu`, monthly
  `0 6 5 * *` Etc/UTC — no `secrets` binding (keyless API).
- `runner.py`: `CONNECTOR_FOR_SOURCE["ted_eu"]="procurement"`;
  `ted_eu_slice` outcome serialization.
- `live_dispositions.toml`: the old `reference` stub row removed —
  connector-mapped sources carry no disposition row (test enforced).

video-surveillance procurement `351100-2025` `can-standard` +
`353033-2025` `cn-standard`) with the i18n field shapes, CPV arrays,

`tests/connectors/test_ted_eu.py` — **22 tests**: target generation +
dedupe, Expert-Search query syntax, field list, CPV/keyword slice kinds,
date bounds, verbatim POST body on the wire, envelope fail-closedness,
i18n extraction, verbatim-literal claims + locators, alpha-3→alpha-2 map
(+ unmapped-code no-fabrication), per-slice outcomes, deterministic
replay/shadow equivalence, 429/disappearance handling, registry loadability
+ gate, no-credential requirement, end-to-end fixture run.
`test_review_status.py` / `test_source_registry.py` baselines updated
(77 loadable; `ted_eu` in `_FLIPPED_SUBSET`).

`make check` green: lint + format + mypy (231 files) + **3,337 passed**
+ verify-gen clean. `sig-connectors validate` green
(198 registered / 77 loadable / 0 flip-ready). `sig-ops cadence --check`
green (every loadable live-target source has a cadence row).

## Local live run — bounded real sweep (pre-hosted proof)

`sig-connectors run --source ted_eu --mode live --sink memory
--capture-dir /tmp/sig-ted-captures` — two runs, 16:18Z + 16:20Z:

- **22 slices, all HTTP 200**, 0 refusals, 0 rate-limit events, 0
  disappearances, 0 drift — ~59 s per run (the reviewed 30/min budget is
  far inside TED's 700/min fair-use limit).
- **69,546 emitted claims**; **identical capture digests across both
  runs** and identical claim count — fetch-level determinism + content
  identity proven before the hosted run.
- Per-slice outcomes recorded honestly: the `video surveillance` seed
  slice returned 250 items of `totalNoticeCount=7068` (`truncated=true`
  — the one-page bound truncates loud); two keyword slices + two CPV
  slices were honest empties; notice rows fetched 0–250 per slice.
- Committed records: `docs/build/reports/live_runs/
  2026-09-18_ted_eu_p2615.json` (+ `_rerun.json`).

## Spine before/after (hosted PG via cloud-sql-proxy `--token`, psycopg)

| measure | before | after run 1 | after run 2 (rerun) | after run 3 (fixed img) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| total `claim` rows | 285,588 | **352,268** (+66,680) | **366,639** (+14,371) | **433,319** (+66,680) |
| `place_of_performance` predicate rows | 0 | 12,717 | 15,525 (+2,808) | 28,242 |
| `country` predicate rows | 0 | 2,844 | 3,452 (+608) | 6,296 |
| `title` predicate rows | 0 | 2,844 | 3,452 (+608) | 6,296 |
| `matched_keyword` predicate rows | 2,182 | 9,038 (+6,856) | 11,112 (+2,074) | 17,968 |
| `products` (CPV) predicate rows | — | 21,516 | 25,306 (+3,790) | 46,064 |
| `seller` predicate rows | — | 3,257 | 3,440 (+183) | 4,355 |
| `description` predicate rows | 1,985 (P26.14) | 4,579 (+2,594) | 5,187 (+608) | 7,781 |
| `external_id` predicate rows | — | 35,038 | 35,646 (+608) | 38,490 |

(`—` = pre-existing rows from the municipal/federal procurement tiers; the
TED-only new predicates are the three zero-before rows.)

**Emitted-vs-spine:** 69,546 emitted → **+66,680** spine rows — the ~2.9k
difference is content-keyed dedupe: overlapping keyword/CPV slices return
the same notices and identical claim content dedupes at insert
(append-only, no overwrite). New notice subjects carry `provenance`
(slice query/keyword/CPV/page + capture digest) and per-field `evidence`
locators (record row in the captured `notices` array; byte range into the
named field for `matched_keyword`).

**Run-2 delta (+14,371) fully attributed:** the only Cloud Run execution
in the measurement window was `nv8kj` itself (every other job's latest
execution predates the run-1 measurement). Of 22 slices, **17 captured
byte-identical payloads** (14 of 19 unique digests shared across runs —
identical `capture_digest` → identical claim digests → **+0** on those
slices, the dedupe mechanism proven on a live feed). The **5 slices
whose payloads changed** (new OJ S publications between the two runs,
~1 h apart) re-asserted their claim sets: claim `evidence` carries the
capture digest (the P26.14 usaspending convention — a claim cites the
exact capture bytes it was extracted from), so changed pages produce
new-digest rows for both genuinely new notices and re-captured ones.
The measured pattern confirms it: every per-notice predicate
(`external_id`/`country`/`title`/`buyer`/`posted_date`/`description`)
grew by exactly **+608** — the distinct new-digest notices on changed
slices — while multi-claim-per-notice predicates grew proportionally
(`products` +3,790, `place_of_performance` +2,808, `matched_keyword`
+2,074). 69,546 emitted → ~55,175 content-identical dedupes +
**14,371 content-keyed new rows** — additions are new evidence, never
silent duplicates (the claim spine is append-only by design).

## Provenance-gap finding + fix (post-run-1)

Inspecting run 1's hosted run row surfaced a real bug: the 21 **generated**
sweep slices' `ted_eu_slice` outcome rows carried
`slice/query_kind/query/ted_keyword/cpv_code = null` (and `cpv_code` would
have surfaced as the literal `"None"`), and every emitted claim's
`evidence.notice_provenance` carried the same nulls. Cause: `discover()`
appended generated targets to the fetch list but never registered them on
`ctx.resolved_targets`, so the post-capture `source_uri` lookup missed
generated slices (the seed slice was unaffected — it is a configured
`live_targets` row). The same latent gap existed for generated
`usaspending`/`sam_gov` slices (P26.14/P26.12) — the fix registers
generated targets on `ctx.resolved_targets` for all three sweeps, the
same mechanism `discover_more` continuations use.

- Fix commit `666fc31` + regression test
  (`test_ted_eu_generated_slice_provenance_resolves_after_discover`);
  `make check` green (3,338 passed).
- **Digest consequence:** `evidence` (which carries `slice` /
  `query_kind` / `ted_keyword` / `cpv_code` / `capture_digest`) is
  inside `content_digest` (`db/claim_sink.py`), so claims emitted by
  the fixed code digest differently than runs 1–2's null-provenance
  claims. A hosted run on the fixed image re-asserts the TED claim set
  as **new rows with richer evidence** — an honest append-only
  correction, not drift. (It also explains part of run 1's
  69,546→66,680 gap: under null slice provenance, a notice hit by both
  a keyword and a CPV slice produced byte-identical claim dicts and
  deduped; under populated provenance those are distinct rows citing
  distinct slices.) Runs 1→2 (same image `af8b878`) remain the
  same-code idempotency proof; run 3 (image built from `666fc31`)
  lands the corrected claim generation + hosted proof of populated
  provenance; the next scheduled run (2026-10-05) dedupes against
  run 3's generation. The identical mechanism applies to the next
  `usaspending`/`sam_gov` hosted runs (same fix, same one-time
  richer-evidence re-assertion).

## Idempotency

- **Rerun `sig-ingest-ted-eu-nv8kj`** (17:28:35Z→18:13:49Z, 45m14s —
  run row `2026-09-18T17-32-29+00-00.json`, `duration_seconds=2472.955`):
  `outcome=ok`, exit 0, **22 captures**, **69,546 emitted** (identical
  count to run 1), 0 refusals / 0 rate-limit events / 0 disappearances /
  0 drift. 14 of 19 unique capture digests shared with run 1 (17 of 22
  slices byte-identical). Spine **+14,371** — see the attribution above:
  unchanged slices deduped to +0; the 5 changed slices' +14,371 are
  content-keyed rows for new OJ S publications and re-captured notices
  (capture-digest-keyed evidence). On a continuously-publishing feed a
  strict whole-run +0 is data-dependent; the mechanism is proven —
  identical claim content inserts zero rows.
- **Run 3 `sig-ingest-ted-eu-59gtq`** (fixed image
  `sig-api@sha256:d5d84b6d`, Cloud Build `61a132ff` from commit
  `666fc31`; 18:24:13Z→19:13:51Z, `duration_seconds=2974.56` ~49m35s):
  `outcome=ok`, exit 0, **22 captures**, **69,546 emitted**, 0 refusals /
  0 rate-limit events / 0 disappearances. **The fix verified hosted:**
  all 22 `ted_eu_slice` outcome rows carry populated provenance
  (`query_kind` = 12 keyword + 10 CPV, `ted_keyword`/`cpv_code`/`query`
  filled; 0 null rows; 4 honest-empty slices) — vs runs 1–2 where the
  21 generated-slice rows were all-null. Spine **+66,680** — the full
  TED claim set re-asserted with richer `evidence` (populated slice
  provenance → new digests): the documented append-only correction,
  not drift. Only 7 of 19 unique digests shared with run 2 — the
  publication surface moved in the ~1.8 h gap (irrelevant to the
  re-assertion, which is keyed on the claim-evidence change). Run 3's
  outcome rows predate the runner-side `slice`-column addition
  (serializer now emits `provenance.slice` too — outcome rows carry
  `url` with the `#sig-slice=` fragment regardless, so slice identity
  was always recoverable). The 2026-10-05 scheduled run dedupes
  against this generation.
